seo.metaTitle: Change PNG Opacity - Make Image Transparent, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Reduce the opacity of a PNG in your browser: the alpha channel is multiplied by a percentage, so 0% is invisible and 100% is unchanged. Free, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Change PNG opacity scales the alpha channel of the whole image, so a fully opaque picture becomes semi-transparent and a 0 percent result is completely invisible. The color channels are left exactly as they were — nothing is blended, every pixel keeps its own color — which is the difference between making an image translucent and making it faded. The result keeps a real alpha channel and drops onto a page, a slide or another image without a white box around it. Everything runs in your browser, so the file is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Alpha is multiplied per pixel; color channels are copied without resampling.
Save as PNG or WebP to keep transparency — JPG flattens it onto a color.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set the opacity percentage: 100 leaves it untouched, 50 makes it half transparent.
Watch the preview against the checkerboard background.
Download the result as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP from the Download button.

faq.q: What is the difference between changing opacity and adding a white background?
faq.a: Opacity touches only the alpha channel, so the picture itself stays pure and keeps its edges. A white background paints over the transparent parts and leaves the pixels underneath untouched - the picture can still look washed out when it sits on another background.

faq.q: Does making an image transparent reduce its quality?
faq.a: No. The alpha value is multiplied per pixel; the color data is copied without resampling. Only the export format matters: save as PNG or WebP to keep transparency, and remember JPG flattens it onto a color.

faq.q: Can I make only part of the image transparent?
faq.a: Not here - this page scales the whole alpha channel. To fade one region, remove that background color first and then apply the opacity to the result.
